graph_nodes.name: S19TuiApp._typed_load_route
examples: (probe p9b U4) `<workarea>/E`, `E` empty → `("refuse", "not a project")` (via the content tail today; via the list match after Q7) (holds on 9a tree)
(probe p9a U3 re-read, code read) a relative folder → `("refuse", "not a supported file")` (LLR-172.5h) (holds on 9a tree)
graph_nodes.func: classifies one typed path from metadata only, never raises: relative → `resolve_input_path`; `None` → `("refuse", "not found")`; a folder → `"not a supported file"`; else by suffix. Absolute → lexical match against the work area (`abspath`, `normcase`), outside: manifest or folder → `"outside"`, file by suffix; inside: `lstat` walk (`"link"`, `"unreadable"`, `"not found"`), one component, matched by `normcase` against `list_projects()` (`"not a project"` when unlisted), then the §1.3 content tail (regular non-link `project.json`, or `validate_project_files` finds data / A2L / an error) → `("project", on-disk name)`. Unchanged by 9b; after Q7 its `list_projects` match already applies §1.3, so the tail becomes a second line of defence.

Reads no content. Unchanged by 9b.

graph_nodes.name: S19TuiApp._handle_load_project
examples: (probe p9b U3, probe p9a U6) `E` (empty) → "Project NOT loaded: 'E' has no project.json — load a file and Save project.", `current_project` `None` (holds on 9a tree; after Q7: "is not a project — pick a project in the list.")

graph_nodes.name: S19TuiApp._parse_loaded_file
examples: (code read, LLR-173.6b) MAC `m.mac` loaded, then data file `f.s19` → installed `LoadedFile` with `path` f.s19 and `mac_path` m.mac (holds on 9a tree)
(code read) no current file, `f.s19` → no MAC, no carried A2L (holds on 9a tree)
graph_nodes.func: the parse used by the worker and by `load_selected_file`: S19 / HEX → parse, then `_merge_primary_with_existing_mac` (the current file's `mac_path`, `mac_records`, `mac_diagnostics` are kept; A2L = the new primary's or else the current one); MAC → `_merge_mac_with_existing_primary` (overlays the MAC on the current S19/HEX, keeps its A2L when the MAC has none). Reads `self.current_file` at parse time (worker thread). This is the "MAC as the install keeps it" of LLR-173.6b, not `_apply_prepared_load`, which only installs the merged `LoadedFile`. Unchanged by 9b.

graph_nodes.name: S19TuiApp._handle_select_variant
examples: (code read, LLR-172.1 9a) the open project's second variant → `0` store writes (holds on 9a tree)

graph_nodes.name: choose_install_set
examples: (code read, LLR-173.6) recorded "v2" in variants v1, v2 → variant v2 (holds on 9a tree)
(code read, LLR-173.6a) recorded "v2", `unreadable` ("v2",) → variant v1 (holds on 9a tree)
graph_nodes.func: pure fallback rule of a project load (LLR-169.6): start at the recorded active variant when it is one of the set, else the first; the first variant not in `unreadable` wins (wrapping once); MAC = the first data file with a MAC suffix; A2L = the first A2L. Called by `_handle_load_project`; its docstring already names "the Load dialog preview (Inc 9b)" as a user. Unchanged by 9b.

graph_nodes.name: resolve_input_path
examples: (probe p9b F6, CR9-1) `R\x.s19`, working directory without `R`, base folder holding `R\x.s19` → `<base>\R\x.s19` (resolved) (holds on 9a tree)
graph_nodes.func: strips spaces and quotes, `expanduser`; the candidate as typed when it exists (relative to the working directory, not resolved); else for a relative path `(base_dir / candidate).resolve()`, then `(repo_root / candidate).resolve()`; else `None`. The fallback hits return a resolved (link-followed) absolute path; the first hit returns the path as typed. Unchanged by 9b (`workspace.py` is outside the cap).

graph_nodes.name: record_recent_source
examples: (probe p9b F6) `<base>\R\x.s19` → `True`; store `[('<base>\R\x.s19', 's19')]` (holds on 9a tree)
graph_nodes.func: records `os.path.abspath(str(path))` first in the per-user store (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\s19_app\recent_sources.json`), de-duplicated by `normcase(abspath)`, capped at 20, atomic replace; never raises; `False` on any skip. Takes no "how was it found" input, so LLR-172.1n's test lives in the caller. Unchanged by 9b.

graph_nodes.name: read_recent_sources
examples: (probe p9b F6/F9) after one outside load and three work-area picks → `1` entry, problem `None` (holds on 9a tree)
graph_nodes.func: the bounded store read: entries (`RecentEntry(path, kind)`, newest first, at most 20) and `problem` (`None`, "too large", "could not be read"; a problem means 0 entries). Never raises; reads no source file. Unchanged by 9b; the dialog's recents section reads it (N1).

graph_nodes.name: recent_kind
examples: (code read) `w.a2l.json` → `None`; `w.A2L` → "a2l" (holds on 9a tree)
graph_nodes.func: pure suffix map with Windows suffix rules: `.s19`/`.srec` → "s19", `.hex`/`.ihex` → "hex", `.mac` → "mac", `.a2l` → "a2l", else `None`. The loadable-suffix filter LLR-173.4b names. Unchanged by 9b.

graph_nodes.name: list_workarea_files
examples: (probe p9b F8) `temp/` with `w.a2l`, `w.a2l.json`, `w.s19`, `x.s19` → all `4` (holds on 9a tree; the filter is the RED side of LLR-173.4b)
graph_nodes.func: the one enumeration of `workarea/temp`: regular, non-link direct children, names ending in "." or " " skipped, sorted by `(casefold, name)`; any `OSError` → `[]`. No suffix filter. Unchanged by 9b; the dialog's files section filters its output by `recent_kind`.

graph_nodes.name: validate_project_files

out.raw: tuple(list[Path] data_files, list[Path] a2l_files, str? error)

examples: (probe p9b U2 setup) `n` holding `notes.txt` → `([], [], None)` (holds on 9a tree)
(probe p9a U2) `temp` holding `firmware.s19` → data `['firmware.s19']` (holds on 9a tree)
graph_nodes.func: scans direct children that are files (`is_file()` follows links): S19 / HEX / MAC → data (sorted `(lower, name)`), A2L → a2l; more than one MAC or A2L → an error text. Raises `OSError` when the folder cannot be listed. With a regular `project.json`, the §1.3 content test of `_typed_load_route`'s tail. Unchanged by 9b.

graph_nodes.name: painted_names
examples: (docstring doctest) `["a", "b‮c"]`, limit `1` → "a, and 1 more" (holds on 9a tree)
graph_nodes.func: the batch's one name scrub: removes Cc, Cf, Zl, Zp characters, turns an unpaired surrogate into U+FFFD, clips each name to `clip` characters ("…"), joins at most `limit` names with ", " then ", and K more". Pure; markup is not parsed (the caller wraps it with `safe_text` or a markup-off widget). Unchanged by 9b.

graph_nodes.name: safe_text
examples: (code read) `"[b]P"` → `Text` with plain "[b]P" and `0` spans (holds on 9a tree)
graph_nodes.func: deletes C0 / C1 control code points and wraps the rest as a Rich `Text` (markup never parsed). Keeps U+202E and surrogates, which is why LLR-173.3 cites `painted_names` and not `safe_text` alone. Unchanged by 9b.
